rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is empty, so the first experiment should test a baseline multimodal configuration to establish performance. This experiment tests combining RNA (pca_n2000) and image (resnet50) encoders with concat fusion, a common approach. It clarifies whether multimodal integration improves performance compared to single-modality baselines, providing critical initial insights.

The existing evidence shows that config_016 (multimodal, concat fusion) achieved 52.66% accuracy. This experiment tests weighted fusion instead of concatenation, a critical design choice that could improve performance. It directly extends the previous experiment to clarify whether fusion method is a key factor, balancing exploration of important decisions without repeating prior configurations.

Existing evidence shows multimodal singleprofile models with pca_n2000 and resnet50 achieve ~0.52 accuracy. This experiment tests replacing resnet50 with the more powerful imagenet_vit_l image encoder while keeping other settings identical (pca_n2000, concat fusion, no aggregation). This clarifies whether the image encoder choice is a critical factor, which remains uncertain. It's a low-risk exploration of a potentially impactful design decision.

Existing evidence shows that using imagenet_vit_l as the image encoder (config_022) achieves the highest validation accuracy (0.535) so far. This experiment tests whether switching from 'concat' to 'weighted' fusion (config_023) improves performance, clarifying the impact of fusion strategies. It directly builds on the strongest image encoder choice while exploring a key design decision with minimal resource cost.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with pca_n2000 RNA encoder and imagenet_vit_l image encoder (config_022) achieve the highest validation accuracy (0.5353). This experiment tests multiprofile setting with avgpool aggregation, which has not been evaluated yet. It clarifies whether the multiprofile setting (more complex) combined with avgpool aggregation could improve performance, building on the current best setup while exploring a key design choice (aggregation method).

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile, pca_n2000 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, avgpool aggregation, and concat fusion achieve the highest validation accuracy (0.628697). This experiment tests whether switching to weighted fusion (instead of concat) with the same setup could further improve performance, clarifying the impact of fusion strategy. It is the best use of the next experiment as it directly builds on the current top-performing configuration to resolve an important design choice with minimal resource cost.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal multiprofile setups with imagenet_vit_l and pca_n2000 encoders, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_025) achieve the highest validation accuracy (0.6352). This experiment tests transformer aggregation with concat fusion, which could reveal if changing the aggregation method further improves performance. It directly addresses uncertainty about the optimal aggregation strategy in this high-performing configuration space.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile, pca_n2000 RNA encoder, and imagenet_vit_l image encoder achieve high validation accuracy (up to 0.6352). This experiment tests whether replacing avgpool aggregation (used in config_025) with transformer aggregation could further improve performance, clarifying if transformer's ability to model complex interactions is beneficial. It directly extends the most promising direction while addressing uncertainty about aggregation methods.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal multiprofile setups with imagenet_vit_l image encoder and avgpool aggregation achieve high validation accuracy (e.g., config_025: 0.6352). This experiment tests whether switching the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200 (a different encoder type) while keeping the high-performing image encoder and aggregation method could further improve performance. This clarifies the importance of RNA encoder choice, a key design decision, without discarding the proven effective components.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder and imagenet_vit_l image encoder (e.g., config_036) achieve high accuracy (0.715). This experiment tests the weighted fusion variant of this setup, clarifying whether fusion method (concat vs weighted) impacts performance. It is the best use of the next experiment as it directly addresses a critical design choice (fusion) in a high-performing configuration, balancing exploitation of promising directions with exploration of key hyperparameters.
